title: Foreign Banks Strengthen Their Business Footprint in Indonesia Through Acquisitions and Integration
body: Several foreign banks are consolidating their positions in Indonesia through acquisitions and business integration to expand customer bases and capture domestic growth opportunities. PT Bank DBS Indonesia (DBSI) became the controlling shareholder of PT DBS Vickers Sekuritas Indonesia (DBSVI) with a 99% stake, serving as the Parent Entity of the DBS Financial Conglomeration in Indonesia. PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk (BDMN) and MUFG Bank Ltd proposed the name PT Bank MUFG Danamon Tbk for their integrated bank, pending shareholder, ministry, and regulator approval. Meanwhile, PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk (NISP) is preparing to take over HSBC Indonesia's retail banking and wealth management assets and liabilities, targeted for completion in Q2-2027 with Rp 89.8 trillion in assets under management transferred. Bank of America Indonesia Country Executive Mira Arifin noted Indonesia's large, young population and the rising cost of independent operations are driving foreign banks toward acquisition-led expansion amid ongoing industry consolidation.

title: 26 Banks Still Below 15% Free Float Requirement; Analysts Weigh Impact on Share Prices
body: As of August 31, 2026, 26 listed banks still have public shareholdings below the 15% free float requirement, with 10 targeting 12.5% by March 31, 2027, two targeting 15% by March 31, 2027, and 14 facing a March 31, 2029 deadline. The lowest free floats include Bank QNB Indonesia (BKSW) at 6.67%, Bank Nationalnobu (NOBU) at 7.34%, Bank Oke Indonesia (DNAR) at 7.53%, Bank Danamon Indonesia (BDMN) at 7.54%, Bank IBK Indonesia (AGRS) at 7.55%, Bank CIMB Niaga (BNGA) at 7.50%, Bank SMBC Indonesia (BTPN) at 7.87%, and Bank Syariah Indonesia (BRIS) at 9.33%, among others. Several banks are preparing corporate actions: BRIS plans a rights issue (PMHMETD II) of up to 6.8 billion Series B shares with Rp500 nominal value, projected to lift capital from Rp51.07 trillion in 2026 to Rp64.41 trillion in 2027 and CAR from 20.38% to 23.31%, with maximum dilution of 12.85% for non-exercising shareholders; CIMB Niaga, Allo Bank Indonesia (BBHI), Super Bank Indonesia (SUPA), Panin Bank, and Bank JTrust Indonesia (BCIC) are also discussing options with controlling shareholders. Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas, RHB Sekuritas Indonesia, and Solstice Indonesia note that new share issuance may cause short-term EPS dilution and supply pressure, while controller share sales avoid dilution but can pressure prices, though higher free float could improve liquidity and broaden the investor base over the medium to long term; for BRIS, one option is partial share sales by shareholders Bank Mandiri (51.47%), BNI (23.24%), and BRI (15.38%).

title: A roundup of 35 acquisition transactions by 29 Indonesia Stock Exchange issuers in 2026 highlights major deals by DSSA, BUMI, TPIA, and SILO across energy, property, and healthcare sectors.
body: The article catalogs 35 acquisition actions undertaken by 29 BEI-listed issuers throughout 2026 up to September 9, spanning sectors including energy, mining, technology, property, financial services, healthcare, infrastructure, logistics, and consumer goods. The largest disclosed transactions include PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) acquiring 100% of PT Bali Media Telekomunikasi for approximately Rp4 trillion followed by an Rp8.54 trillion capital injection, PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) planning the acquisition of 14 hospital facility entities valued around Rp9 trillion, and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) pursuing the purchase of Cycle & Carriage automotive businesses in Singapore and Malaysia for about US$207 million (Rp3.68 trillion). Other significant deals feature PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) completing the acquisition of Australian copper-gold miner Loyal Metals Ltd for Rp1,004 trillion via its subsidiary Bumi Resources Australia, PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) acquiring 99.99% of PT Kemilau Mulia Sakti for Rp1.73 trillion, and PT Harta Djaya Karya Tbk (MEJA) processing a 45% stake in PT Trimitra Coal Perkasa for Rp1.6 trillion. Financial sector activity includes PT Bank Maybank Indonesia Tbk (BNII) acquiring 51% stakes in PT Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia (Rp583.74 billion) and PT Maybank Asset Management (Rp5.35 billion), while PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk (NISP) plans to take 98.99% of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia for Rp453.45 billion. Property and infrastructure deals involve PT Pakuan Tbk (UANG) buying two property firms for Rp45 billion and Rp156 billion, PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) raising its stake in PT Bach Multi Global Tbk (BACH) to 51% for Rp460.7 billion, and PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) acquiring 55% each in two maritime firms for about Rp550 million each.

title: Indonesia's gigawatt-scale data centre expansion requires financing beyond bank lending, experts say
body: Indonesia's target to reach 1.7 gigawatts of data centre capacity by 2026 translates to an estimated US$17 billion investment need, which industry leaders say exceeds the lending capacity of banks alone. Recent syndicated loans include Rp6.7 trillion from Bank DBS Indonesia and Bank UOB Indonesia for the DayOne-INA campus in Batam, Rp17 trillion from PT Bank Central Asia Tbk for PT DCI Indonesia Tbk in May 2026, and Rp8.8 trillion from a syndicate of PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk, PT Bank HSBC Indonesia, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk for STT GDC Indonesia in June 2026. JPMorgan Indonesia CEO Gioshia Ralie states that bank financing has inherent limits and must be combined with capital market instruments, a view echoed by IDPRO Chairman Hendra Suryakusuma, who notes that bank loans remain crucial for construction but that operational assets can attract institutional investors, infrastructure funds, and green financing. Gioshia adds that this blended financing model is already established in the United States and can be replicated in Indonesia.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk completes acquisition of 20% stake in PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia for Rp201.98 billion
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk, acting as the Perusahaan Induk Konglomerasi Keuangan (PIKK), completed the purchase of a 20% equity stake, including one preferred share, in PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia for Rp201.98 billion. The share purchase and takeover deeds were signed on 1 September 2026, giving OCBC NISP control over GELI despite the minority holding. The acquisition follows a Conditional Sale and Purchase Agreement with The Great Eastern Life Assurance Company Limited and supports OCBC NISP’s plan to build an OCBC Group financial conglomerate in Indonesia, adding life‑insurance capabilities to its banking business. OCBC NISP disclosed that the transaction will not have a material impact on its operations or continuity.

title: Sukuk Ritel SR025 Offering Surpasses Rp 9 Trillion in Two Weeks
body: The Ministry of Finance’s Sukuk Ritel series SR025 has attracted more than Rp 9 trillion in orders within the first two weeks of its 21 August 2026 launch. By 4 September 2026, orders totalled about Rp 9.6 trillion, comprising roughly Rp 8 trillion for the 3‑year SR025T3 series (6.8% coupon) and Rp 1.6 trillion for the 5‑year SR025T5 series (6.9% coupon), leaving a remaining quota of about Rp 10.4 trillion. The offering, which closes on 16 September 2026, is being sold through 33 designated distribution partners, including PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk, PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank DBS Indonesia, PT Bank HSBC Indonesia, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Maybank Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Mega Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk, PT Bank Panin Tbk, PT Bank Permata Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk, PT Bank UOB Indonesia, Standard Chartered Bank, PT Bank Victoria International, PT Bank SMBC Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Muamalat Indonesia Tbk, PT BRI Danareksa Sekuritas, PT Mandiri Sekuritas, PT Trimegah Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk, PT Bahana Sekuritas, PT Binaartha Sekuritas, PT Phillip Sekuritas Indonesia, PT BNI Sekuritas, PT Panin Sekuritas Tbk, PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia, PT Bareksa Portal Investasi, PT Nusantara Sejahtera Investama, PT Star Mercato Capitale, and PT Bibit Tumbuh Bersama. These partners act as the government‑designated distribution channels for the sukuk, handling online registration, order placement, payment processing, and allocation confirmation.

title: Bank OCBC NISP completes acquisition of Great Eastern Life Indonesia for Rp 201.98 billion
body: Bank OCBC NISP completed the acquisition of PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia, purchasing a 20% stake for Rp 201.98 billion, which includes a preferred share that gives the bank full control of the insurer. The transaction finalised on 1 September 2026 under the Conditional Sale and Purchase Agreement signed on 8 June 2026, and positions Bank OCBC NISP as the Parent Company of the OCBC Group Financial Conglomerate in Indonesia, with Great Eastern Life Indonesia becoming a member of the conglomerate. The Great Eastern Life Assurance Company Limited acted as the counter‑party in the share purchase agreement. Following the announcement, Bank OCBC NISP’s shares closed up 0.4% at Rp 1,250, and management said the deal will not have a material negative impact on operations, legal matters, financial condition, or business continuity.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk acquires controlling stake in PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia for Rp201.98 billion
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk completed the acquisition of a 20 % equity stake and one preferred share in PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia, giving it control over the insurer, in a transaction valued at Rp201.98 billion. The deal follows a Conditional Sale and Purchase Agreement dated 8 July 2026 between the parties and is intended to expand the OCBC financial conglomerate in Indonesia, with PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk acting as the parent of the new financial group. After the announcement, PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk’s shares opened at Rp1,255, up 0.80 % and reflecting a price‑to‑earnings multiple of 5.27× based on an annualized earnings per share of Rp237.97.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk acquires 20% of PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia for Rp201.98 billion
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk announced the acquisition of a 20.00 % stake in PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia for a total consideration of Rp201.98 billion, which includes one preferred share that confers control. The transaction was formalized by signing Share Purchase Agreement No. 1 and Acquisition Deed No. 3 on 1 September 2026, with legal approval from the Ministry of Law effective 1–2 September 2026 and disclosed to the Indonesia Stock Exchange on 3 September 2026. OCBC will serve as the Financial Conglomerate Holding Company (PIKK) of the newly formed OCBC Group financial conglomerate, with PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia becoming a member of the conglomerate. The company stated that the acquisition does not have a material impact on its operational activities or business continuity.

title: Performance Review of Indonesia’s 10 Largest Banks Shows BTN Leads Profit Growth in H1 2026
body: The article reviews the H1‑2026 results of Indonesia’s ten largest banks—Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA, CIMB Niaga, Bank Permata, Bank Danamon, Bank OCBC NISP, Bank Syariah Indonesia and BTN—highlighting overall resilience despite tighter funding costs. BTN posted the highest year‑on‑year profit growth at 40.80%, reaching Rp2.40 trillion, while BRI recorded the largest absolute profit of Rp31.18 trillion and Danamon posted a 33.05% increase to Rp2.39 trillion. All banks except CIMB Niaga reported profit expansion, with credit growth remaining in double‑digit range (e.g., BRI +16.16% to Rp1,646 trillion, Mandiri +19.90% to Rp1,592 trillion) and third‑party funds (DPK) rising notably for BNI (+22.26%) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (+21.81%). Analysts note that despite solid fundamentals, Himbara bank stocks have underperformed YTD, reflecting pressure on net interest margins and foreign outflows, but they remain optimistic about further credit‑driven profit upside in H2 2026.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk expands retail wealth‑management services and highlights Rp 89.8 trillion AUM acquisition from HSBC Indonesia
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk is broadening its wealth‑management business to the retail segment by launching digital tools such as For Your Investment (FYI), Financial Fitness Check Up (FFCU) and Life Goals, which allow investments as low as Rp 10,000. The bank says the new features aim to shift customers from conservative to more aggressive risk profiles and enable early wealth accumulation. OCBC previously acquired the assets and liabilities of HSBC Indonesia’s retail banking and wealth‑management business, adding Rp 89.8 trillion of assets under management. The acquisition positions OCBC as the acquirer of HSBC Indonesia’s wealth‑management assets, while HSBC Indonesia is the target of that transaction. These moves are part of OCBC’s strategy to make wealth management more inclusive for Indonesian retail customers.

title: Government launches SR025 retail Sukuk with fixed coupons of 6.80% (3‑year) and 6.90% (5‑year)
body: The Indonesian Ministry of Finance announced the retail issuance of SR025 Sukuk series T3 (3‑year) and T5 (5‑year) with fixed coupons of 6.80% and 6.90% per annum, respectively, available for order online from 21 August to 16 September. The securities will begin secondary‑market trading on 11 October 2026 after the minimum holding period expires. The offering is distributed through thirty‑three designated partners, including PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk, PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank DBS Indonesia, PT Bank HSBC Indonesia, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Maybank Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Mega Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk, PT Bank Panin Tbk, PT Bank Permata Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk, PT Bank UOB Indonesia, Standard Chartered Bank, PT Bank Victoria International, PT Bank SMBC Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Muamalat Indonesia Tbk, PT BRI Danareksa Sekuritas, PT Mandiri Sekuritas, PT Trimegah Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk, PT Bahana Sekuritas, PT Binaartha Sekuritas, PT Phillip Sekuritas Indonesia, PT BNI Sekuritas, PT Panin Sekuritas Tbk, PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia, PT Bareksa Portal Investasi, PT Nusantara Sejahtera Investama (FUNDtastic+), PT Star Mercato Capitale (Tanamduit), and PT Bibit. These partners will handle registration, order placement, payment and ownership confirmation via the e‑SBN platform.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk completes Rp455 billion acquisition of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia, forming financial conglomerate
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk completed the acquisition of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia. The transaction, valued at Rp455.2 billion, became effective on 13 August 2026 and gave the bank direct control of 99.99% of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia, making it a subsidiary. PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk will act as the Parent Company of the Financial Conglomerate (PIKK) with PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia as a member, aiming to strengthen integration of banking and securities services. The bank stated the deal has no material adverse impact on its operations, legal standing, financial condition, or business continuity.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk completes Rp455.2 billion acquisition of 99.9999% of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk finalized the purchase of 99,9999% of PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia. The transaction was valued at Rp455,201 billion. Prior to the deal, the shares were held by Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited (98,9932%), PT Farnella Mandiri Utama (0,6244%) and PT OCBC NISP Ventura (0,3823%); the acquisition received OJK approval (Letter S-294/PM.11/2026 dated 24 June 2026) and became effective on 13 August 2026. The move integrates PT OCBC Sekuritas Indonesia into the OCBC financial conglomerate, with PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk acting as the parent entity.

title: Liquidity in Indonesian banking sector tightens, with LDRs of major banks increasing in the first half of 2026
body: The article reports that banking liquidity in Indonesia is becoming tighter, as reflected by rising loan‑to‑deposit ratios (LDR) among several large banks in the first half of 2026. Industry‑wide LDR stood at 86.63% in May 2026, while deposit growth (DPK) rose 13.47% year‑on‑year. Individual banks saw LDR increases: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (78.7% up from 78%), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (92.7% up from 90.2%), PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (96.6% up from 92.6%), PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk (76.3% up from 76%), PermataBank (90.3% up from 85.6%), and Allo Bank (163.86% up from 128.73%). Executives from the banks and the LPPI noted that despite tighter ratios, liquidity remains adequate due to macro‑prudential measures such as the KLM policy and strong CASA growth at BCA.

title: KBMI 3 banks post profit growth in H1‑2026, highlighting top performers
body: KBMI 3 banks posted profit growth in the first half of 2026, with varying degrees of expansion. PT Bank Permata Tbk reported net profit of Rp 1.7 trillion (+4.5% YoY) on credit of Rp 171.2 trillion (+5.3% YoY) and a 4.1% decline in net interest income; PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk posted net profit of Rp 2.7 trillion (+6.4% YoY) on credit of Rp 184.76 trillion (+11.4% YoY) and a 7.24% rise in NII; PT Bank Maybank Indonesia Tbk recorded net profit of Rp 698.7 billion (+21.2% YoY) on credit of Rp 126.3 trillion (+3.8% YoY); PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk achieved net profit of Rp 2.4 trillion (+33% YoY) on credit of Rp 187 trillion (+13.9% YoY); PT Bank Pan Indonesia Tbk saw net profit fall 1.2% to Rp 1.4 trillion as credit contracted 6.1% to Rp 139.6 trillion. All banks also reported changes in net interest income, commission revenue and third‑party funds, with OCBC NISP and Maybank showing strong commission growth, while Panin’s commission fell 10.7%. Management highlighted strategies such as Permata’s partnership with Bangkok Group, OCBC’s wealth‑management focus, Maybank’s risk‑management emphasis, and Danamon’s double‑digit profit drive.

title: Bank OCBC NISP posts Rp2.7 trillion net profit in H1 2026, up 6% YoY
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk reported a net profit of Rp2.7 trillion for the first half of 2026, representing a 6 % year‑on‑year increase. Total operating revenue rose 6 % to Rp6.9 trillion while operating expenses grew 1 % to Rp3.1 trillion. The bank’s credit portfolio expanded 11 % to Rp185.3 trillion and total deposits reached Rp239.9 trillion, with CASA growing 26 % to Rp145.2 trillion and a CASA ratio of 60.5 %. Asset base grew 11 % to Rp329.5 trillion, equity to Rp44.4 trillion, and the institution maintained strong capital and liquidity metrics (CAR 23.1 %, LCR 233.2 %) alongside a low NPL gross of 1.9 % and an improved loan‑at‑risk ratio of 4.8 %.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk reports net profit of Rp2.73 trillion in H1 2026
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk posted a net profit of Rp2.73 trillion for the first half of 2026. The profit rose 6% year‑on‑year, supported by net interest income of Rp5.85 trillion (up 7%) and credit disbursements of Rp185.3 trillion (up 11%). Total assets reached Rp329.5 trillion (up 11%) and equity Rp44.4 trillion (up 8%), with a capital adequacy ratio of 23.1% and liquidity coverage ratio of 233.2%; the gross non‑performing loan ratio was 1.9% and Loan at Risk improved to 4.8%. CASA balances grew to Rp145.2 trillion, a 26% increase, lifting the CASA ratio to 60.5%. President Director Parwati Surjaudaja said the results strengthen the bank’s foundation for sustainable growth and expansion of wealth‑management services.

title: Foreign banks accelerate corporate actions to meet financial conglomerate regulations
body: The article reports that several foreign banks in Indonesia are rapidly undertaking corporate actions to comply with the Financial Conglomerate and Parent Financial Conglomerate (PIKK) regulations. PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk obtained OJK approval to become the controlling shareholder of PT Great Eastern Life Indonesia, acquiring a 20 % stake that will raise OCBC Indonesia’s total assets from Rp 308.14 trillion to Rp 323.72 trillion as of 31 December 2025. PT Bank Maybank Indonesia Tbk is preparing to acquire the shares of its sister firms PT Maybank Asset Management, PT Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia and PT Asuransi Etiqa Internasional Indonesia, after shareholder approval, and will position itself as the parent of a conglomerate that includes PT Maybank Indonesia Finance and PT Wahana Ottomitra Multiartha Tbk (WOM Finance). PT Bank Danamon Indonesia Tbk received a mandate to act as the operational PIKK for the MUFG Financial Conglomerate in Indonesia, integrating with MUFG Cabang Indonesia and overseeing members PT Adira Dinamika Multi Finance Tbk, PT Home Credit Indonesia and PT Mandala Multi Finance Tbk. PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk is noted as focusing on its existing businesses while monitoring organic expansion opportunities under the same regulatory framework.

title: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk reports net profit of Rp 2.7 trillion in H1 2026, credit and deposits up 11%
body: PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk posted a net profit of Rp 2.7 trillion for the first half of 2026. Its credit portfolio reached Rp 185.3 trillion and DPK grew to Rp 239.9 trillion, both up 11% year‑on‑year. Total revenue rose 6% to Rp 6.9 trillion while operating expenses increased only 1% to Rp 3.1 trillion, supporting an 11% increase in total assets to Rp 329.5 trillion and an 8% rise in equity to Rp 44.4 trillion. Asset quality remained solid with gross NPL at 1.9% and a provision coverage of 230%, and capital adequacy and liquidity ratios stood at 23.1% and 233.2% respectively. Digital engagement grew, with e‑channel transaction value up 15% YoY and active internet banking/OCBC Mobile users up 6% and OCBC Business users up 23% YoY, highlighting the bank’s focus on wealth management and digital capabilities.
